pr_title: drivers: rtc: sam0: Optimize RTC register access
pr_body:
The driver issues a READREQ for every access to the COUNT register which causes 180us of delay.  This is a large delay that causes several problems with other systems including i2c and power management.

This commit uses continuous read requests (RCONT) to optimize accessing the COUNT register.  This reduces (but does not eliminate) the time spent synchronizing the COUNT register.

This commit also prevent interrupts from corrupting COUNT and COMP register access.

The kernel does not like it when the RTC does not tick after waking from sleep. RCONT enables continuously syncing the COUNT register but after sleep, we need to wait for a new read request to complete. However, the SYNCBUSY flag is not set when RCONT is enabled so we cannot use that to do the sync. So, we wait for the RTC COUNT register to begin ticking again by reading the COUNT register.

We should wait a minimum of the TICK_THRESHOLD which is the amount of time it takes to sync the register.

Fixes #21549
Fixes #21114
Fixes #21092

issue_context.title: i2c-sam0 sleeps waiting for interrupt
comments:
I have another observation regarding the sam0 i2c driver.  It appears that the i2c bus can be left in a non idle state.  This is a problem because the SCL and/or SDA lines can be held low by the sam0 during and after sleep resulting in significant current (>500uA) due to the pull up resistors on these lines.

I have not isolated what is causing this issue but I have confirmed using an oscilloscope that the SCL and/or SDA lines remain low after an i2c transaction.

It is possible this issue is not related to the topic of this issue and should be a recorded as a separate issue.

review_comments:
Do you mean to match the TICK_THRESHOLD?  The actual delay is 6 GCLK + 3 APB cycles.  Generally, APB >> GCLK.  However, if for some reason, they were the same, then the delay would be equivalent to 9 cycles.  I believe the original author assumed APB >> GCLK and "rounded up" to 7 GCLK cycles.

Do you want me to clarify that or change the threshold?

/*
 * Due to the nature of clock synchronization, reading from or writing to some
 * RTC registers takes approximately six RTC_GCLK cycles.
 *
 * The actual delay is 6 GCLK + 3 APB cycles. Generally, APB >> GCLK.
 * However, if for some reason, the clocks were the same, then the delay would
 * be equivalent to 9 cycles.
 * 
 * We will assume APB >> GCLK and "round up" to 7 GCLK cycles.
 * The worst case update time after sleep requires 2 sync busy synchronizations.
 * Thus, the threshold is 7 x 2 = 14 cycles.
 *
 * This constant defines a safe threshold for the comparator.
 */
Ditto.  Optionally, put both line 117 and 118 into a single `|=`

I do not think you can combine these into one operation.  The datasheet does appear to indicate that RCONT must be written before the RREQ bit.
_For the continuous read mode, RREQ bit is required to be set once the RCONT bit is set._

I think in my experimentation, I attempted to combine them.  If I recall, it does not work reliably if you do.

Overall, the entire RCONT functionality is poorly documented.

I should also mention these changes only affect the SAM D.  I do not presently have SAM E hardware to do testing of the RCONT function for that device.  I reviewed the SAM E datasheet and believe the RCONT functionality may be different.
  
So, these changes are targeting the SAM D only at the moment.

This commit seems unrelated to the RTC fix.  Please split it out.

These changes are related and required because a special synchronization is required when coming out of the STANDBY sleep state.  Specifically, _sys_pm_power_state_exit_post_ops() provides a busy wait until the RTC starts ticking again.
